name: Work across two clusters with contexts
objective: CKA exam-environment skill: every task names the cluster to target. Drill the whole multi-cluster surface harder than the exam — switch contexts, create on the right cluster (never the wrong one), set a context's default namespace, copy a live resource across clusters with get|apply, inspect contexts, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix of a resource built on the WRONG cluster. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Switch context and act on the right cluster
questions.teach:
`kubectl config use-context <name>` switches the **active context** — the cluster every later `kubectl` lands on. You have `kind-kindlab` (`$CTX`) and `kind-kindlab2` (`$CTX2`). Confirm with `kubectl config get-contexts`: the `*` marks the active one.

**Shell tip:** switching context stays in the *same shell*, so your `alias k` / `export do` **persist** across clusters — set them once. They only reset if you `ssh` to a node; add them to `~/.bashrc` to survive new terminal tabs.

**Gotcha:** a correct command on the wrong cluster grades wrong — this step requires `prod` on cluster2 and NOT on cluster1.
questions.prompt:
Switch to the **second** cluster and create namespace `prod` **there** (`$CTX2`), not on cluster1.

Target: namespace `prod` exists on cluster2 and does NOT exist on cluster1.
questions.hint: `kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab2` then `kubectl create namespace prod` — or one-shot: `kubectl --context kind-kindlab2 create ns prod`.
questions.solution:
kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab2
kubectl create namespace prod
kubectl config get-contexts   # confirm the * is on kind-kindlab2

questions.title: Deploy onto cluster2 (one safe command)
questions.teach:
Scope a single command to one cluster AND namespace with `--context` and `-n` together: `kubectl --context $CTX2 -n prod create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=2`. This never touches your active context.

**Gotcha:** omit `-n` and the Deployment lands in the context's default namespace (usually `default`), not the one you meant.
questions.prompt:
On cluster2, create a Deployment `api` (image `nginx:alpine`, 2 replicas) in the `prod` namespace.

Target: Deployment `api` with image `nginx:alpine` and 2 replicas exists in `prod` on cluster2.
questions.solution: kubectl --context kind-kindlab2 -n prod create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=2

verification.description: Deployment 'api' (nginx:alpine, 2 replicas) in prod on cluster2

questions.title: Now work on cluster1
questions.teach:
Switching back to cluster1 is just another `use-context kind-kindlab`. Create a ConfigMap imperatively: `kubectl create configmap <name> --from-literal=key=value`.

**Gotcha:** the clusters are fully independent — the ConfigMap you make on cluster1 does NOT exist on cluster2.
questions.prompt:
Switch to **cluster1** (`$CTX`) and create a ConfigMap `shared-cfg` with key `env=prod` in the `default` namespace **there**.

Target: `shared-cfg` (env=prod) exists in default on cluster1 and NOT in default on cluster2.
questions.hint: `kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab` then `kubectl create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod`.
questions.solution:
kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab
kubectl create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod

verification.description: configmap 'shared-cfg' (env=prod) in default on cluster1 only

questions.title: Copy a live resource across clusters (get | apply)
questions.teach:
To clone an object onto another cluster, pipe it: `kubectl --context $CTX get configmap shared-cfg -o yaml | kubectl --context $CTX2 -n prod apply -f -`.

**Gotcha:** a raw `get -o yaml` carries `resourceVersion`/`uid`/`namespace` — override the target with `-n prod` on apply, or just recreate imperatively.
questions.prompt:
Replicate `shared-cfg` (env=prod) from cluster1 into the `prod` namespace on **cluster2** — same key/value.

Target: ConfigMap `shared-cfg` with `env=prod` exists in `prod` on cluster2.
questions.hint: Simplest that always works: `kubectl --context kind-kindlab2 -n prod create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod`. Or pipe `get -o yaml` from cluster1 into `apply -f -` on cluster2 with `-n prod`.
questions.solution: kubectl --context kind-kindlab2 -n prod create configmap shared-cfg --from-literal=env=prod

verification.description: shared-cfg (env=prod) exists in prod on cluster2

questions.title: Set a context's default namespace
questions.teach:
A context pins cluster+user+**namespace**. Set the default namespace so you stop typing `-n`: `kubectl config set-context kind-kindlab2 --namespace=prod`. Now bare commands on that context hit `prod`.

**Gotcha:** `set-context --current` edits whatever is active now — name the context explicitly (`kind-kindlab2`) so you edit the right one regardless of where you're standing.
questions.prompt:
Set the **default namespace** of the `$CTX2` context to `prod` (so `kubectl --context $CTX2 get pods` with no `-n` targets `prod`).

Target: context `kind-kindlab2` has `namespace: prod` in the kubeconfig.
questions.hint: `kubectl config set-context kind-kindlab2 --namespace=prod`. Confirm with `kubectl config get-contexts` (NAMESPACE column).
questions.solution:
kubectl config set-context kind-kindlab2 --namespace=prod
kubectl config get-contexts

questions.title: A Secret only on cluster1 (independence)
questions.teach:
Secrets, like every object, live in exactly one cluster. Create a generic Secret on cluster1: `kubectl --context $CTX -n default create secret generic <name> --from-literal=k=v`.

**Gotcha:** making it on cluster1 does NOT propagate to cluster2 — this step requires it present on cluster1 and absent on cluster2.
questions.prompt:
On **cluster1** (`$CTX`), create a generic Secret `db-cred` in `default` with key `password=s3cr3t`.

Target: Secret `db-cred` with `password=s3cr3t` exists in default on cluster1 and does NOT exist in default on cluster2.
questions.hint: `kubectl --context kind-kindlab -n default create secret generic db-cred --from-literal=password=s3cr3t`.
questions.solution: kubectl --context kind-kindlab -n default create secret generic db-cred --from-literal=password=s3cr3t

verification.description: secret 'db-cred' (password=s3cr3t) in default on cluster1 only

questions.title: Context discipline — know where you are
questions.teach:
Finish each task by leaving your active context where the *next* one expects, then verify with `kubectl config current-context`. Set it back to cluster1 with `kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab`.

**Gotcha:** `use-context` persists to the kubeconfig file, so your choice survives into the next task's shell — set it deliberately rather than assuming.
questions.prompt:
Leave your **active** context set to cluster1 (`$CTX`).

Target: `kubectl config current-context` returns `kind-kindlab`.
questions.solution:
kubectl config use-context kind-kindlab
kubectl config current-context   # kind-kindlab
